entries.title: Add many papers to your library at once
entries.body: Drop or choose several files on your library and each is added as a short record of its title, authors, abstract and DOI, with progress shown, duplicates spotted, and Stop and Retry to hand. These papers are marked as not yet read by the AI; press Read this on one when you want the full treatment. To find those details, the opening pages of each PDF go to an AI service, as the privacy policy now says.

entries.title: Structure can show the whole piece expanded
entries.body: Structure has an Expanded view beside Fisheye: every part and section of the piece, each with its summary, in one scrolling list that keeps pace with where you are reading. With Structure open, the left and right arrow keys step between the smallest sections, and the up and down keys move one passage at a time.

entries.title: Summary is simpler and skips the paperwork
entries.body: Summary is now just its Brief to Fuller slider, in a slightly wider panel; its parts-and-sections outline has gone, as Structure covers it. Summaries and the Tweets thread leave out author lists, acknowledgements, funding and disclosures, and end on the piece's conclusion. Summaries written before this show as out of date.

entries.title: A Sketch is ready in about a minute
entries.body: Drawing a Sketch usually takes about a minute, and the progress card says so; it calls the step slow only after 3 minutes. We changed how the AI works on it, and in a blind comparison the drawings looked no worse.

entries.title: Chat sees your screen; Citations searches the web
entries.body: A question sent in Chat tells the AI which passages were on your screen, as context only, so ‘this’ or ‘here’ can point where you meant. In Citations, Investigate is renamed Dig deeper: each press searches the web, and your own library, before answering, and answers have more room before being cut short.

entries.title: Glossary terms stand out from internal links
entries.body: Glossary terms have a heavier dotted underline, and links to other passages of the same piece a thin grey one that takes the link colour when you point at it, so the two are easy to tell apart. Pointing at the reading-time line in the margin opens a card explaining what it shows.

entries.title: Tables and multi-panel figures appear in PDFs
entries.body: Tables in an added PDF arrived as a caption over an empty box; their contents now appear as a table under the caption. Figures made of several panels, or drawn rather than pasted in, can be shown too, when the app is sure the picture belongs to its caption. This applies to PDFs added from now on.

entries.title: Dictation uses your computer's chosen microphone
entries.body: With no microphone picked, dictation and live conversation could open the browser's own default rather than the one your computer is set to use. They use your system's choice now, the dictation strip names the microphone the whole time it listens, and a picked microphone that has gone missing falls back to the system default.
